newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Senate committee passes MMT ban bill.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Senate committee passes MMT ban bill.

text.p: The Canadian Senate's energy committee passed a bill on Tuesday that would effectively ban the gasoline additive MMT.
The government bill had already passed the House of Commons, Parliament's elected chamber, and now only required a final passage in the unelected Senate.
A Senate spokeswoman said the Senate as a whole would take up the bill next Tuesday.
Ethyl Corp makes MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl tricarbonyl, and its Canadian subsidiary imports it.
MMT boosts octane and has been used as a replacement for lead in Canada since 1977, but the auto industry and environmentalists have lobbied to ban it.
Ethyl said last year it would sue the Canadian government for US$200 million under the North American Free Trade Agreement if the ban went ahead.
It argued the bill was a trade rather than health or environmental measure since MMT would still in theory be allowed to be made in Canada as long as it did not cross provincial borders.
